title: Opportunities for Chemical Companies in the AI Infrastructure Boom
gist: BCG argues the chemicals downcycle's best escape route is electronic chemicals and materials—a $75B+ TAM tied to AI accelerators, advanced packaging, thermal management and robotics, where niches compound at 5-10% CAGR with 20%+ EBITDA and delivered 15% median annual TSR from 2020-2024 versus 7% for chemicals overall. The moat is customer qualification rather than scale, which makes narrow bolt-on M&A with light-touch integration the only workable entry, with Entegris as the template.

themes.theme: Chemicals downcycle pivots to AI-linked materials

insights.claim: The global chemicals industry is in a downcycle, and BCG's research points the sector's growth-starved incumbents toward electronic chemicals and materials as the most compelling place to buy into an expanding, profitable market.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Expect commodity/petrochemical names to justify premium multiples paid for electronic-materials assets; watch chemicals M&A announcements skew to semis exposure.
insights.locator: Given the current downcycle in the global chemicals industry

insights.claim: Several sectors within electronic chemicals and materials are expected to compound at 5-10% CAGR through 2030 with EBITDA margins above 20%, far above bulk-chemical economics.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A quantified hurdle rate for judging whether a chemicals company's electronics pivot is actually accretive.
insights.quote: several sectors in this space are expected to see CAGRs of 5 to 10 percent to 2030, with EBITDA margins in excess of 20 percent.
insights.locator: Given the current downcycle in the global chemicals industry

insights.claim: Electronic chemicals and materials delivered a 15% median annual TSR from 2020 through 2024, versus 7% for the global chemicals industry and about 10% across all industries.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Backtested evidence that the semis-materials sleeve, not diversified chemicals, is where shareholder returns have been; a screen for relative-value pairs within chemicals.
insights.quote: electronic chemicals and materials having delivered a 15% median annual TSR from 2020 through 2024—compared to 7% across the global chemicals industry and around 10% across all industries
insights.locator: And the returns are attractive

insights.claim: The total addressable market for electronic chemicals and materials across the semiconductor supply chain is over $75 billion today, with AI and advanced computing as incremental growth drivers on top of that base.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Sizes the pool: a $75B+ base means even niche 1-2% share positions are material for mid-cap specialty chemical companies.
insights.locator: The total addressable market for electronic chemicals

themes.theme: AI capex cascading into physical inputs

insights.claim: Worldwide spending on AI is expected to exceed $2.5 trillion in 2026, according to Gartner.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The top-of-funnel number any AI-derivative demand model for materials, power, or packaging has to be anchored to.
insights.quote: Worldwide spending on AI is expected to exceed $2.5 trillion in 2026, according to Gartner
insights.locator: The AI Boom Is Creating New Opportunities

insights.claim: CEOs surveyed by BCG say corporate AI investment will roughly double as a share of revenues, from 0.8% in 2025 to about 1.7% in 2026.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A budget-intensity metric to track: if the 0.8%-to-1.7% step-up slips, the whole AI-infrastructure demand chain de-rates from the top down.
insights.quote: the CEOs we surveyed saying corporate AI investment will double as a share of revenues, from 0.8% in 2025 to about 1.7% in 2026
insights.locator: The AI Boom Is Creating New Opportunities

insights.claim: AI demand is cascading beyond software into supporting infrastructure—microchips, memory, and storage—and each of those layers consumes specialized chemicals such as photoresist, wet chemicals, and thermally conductive adhesives.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Frames the investable chain three steps below the model layer, where competition is narrower than in GPUs.
insights.locator: This growth will be generated primarily by accelerating demand for AI

insights.claim: The shift to advanced-node chip technology mechanically increases materials intensity per chip, so electronic-chemicals demand grows faster than semiconductor unit volumes alone would imply.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Materials suppliers get a node-migration multiplier on top of volume growth—a reason their revenue can outgrow wafer starts.
insights.quote: a shift to advanced node technology in microchips, which requires more materials
insights.locator: Demand for electronic chemicals and materials in this market is growing rapidly

insights.claim: Rising computation density inside data centers is generating incremental demand for thermal management solutions and for auxiliary services around utilities and power generation, extending the opportunity beyond the chip itself.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Thermal and power adjacencies are a second, less-crowded way to own AI buildout exposure than semis equipment.
insights.locator: The opportunity also extends well beyond microchips

insights.claim: Embodied AI and robotics create a distinct materials demand pool—specialized polymers, lightweight structures, sensors, and engineered plastics—separate from the semiconductor value chain.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: An optionality leg: robotics materials demand is not yet priced into most specialty polymer names.
insights.locator: In addition, embodied AI and robotics rely on specialized polymers

insights.claim: Simultaneous expansion of electronics manufacturing in Asia, the US, and the EU is itself a demand driver for electronic chemicals, layering regional duplication on top of underlying volume growth.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Fab regionalization means the same wafer demand supports more local chemical capacity—favors suppliers with multi-region footprints.
insights.locator: and to expanding electronics manufacturing in Asia, the US, and the EU

insights.claim: Systems built around leading-edge GPUs can cost tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars, and the specialized chemicals used to build them directly determine yield, reliability, and throughput—so materials carry pricing power disproportionate to their share of the bill of materials.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Explains why 20%+ EBITDA margins persist in these niches: the cost of a yield loss dwarfs the price of the chemical.
insights.locator: Systems built around leading-edge GPUs can cost tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars

themes.theme: Segment economics: where the AI beta actually sits

insights.claim: AI-linked demand is concentrated in the semiconductor front end and advanced packaging; other electronic-chemicals areas are less levered to AI because they carry broader end-market exposure or less AI-driven innovation.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A filter against 'AI-washing': check whether an electronic-materials asset sits in front end or advanced packaging before paying an AI multiple.
insights.locator: AI-linked demand is primarily concentrated in the semiconductor value chain

insights.claim: Lithography and its ancillaries generated more than $5 billion of revenue in 2025, with a projected 10% CAGR to 2030 and around 20% EBITDA margins.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Concrete size-growth-margin triangle for the most yield-critical patterning step; a benchmark for pricing any litho-chemicals acquisition.
insights.quote: lithography and its ancillaries, which had revenues of more than $5 billion in 2025, a 10% CAGR projected to 2030, and around 20% EBITDA
insights.locator: Example Attractive Plays

insights.claim: Thermal interface materials were an approximately $2 billion market in 2025 with a 10% CAGR to 2030 and EBITDA margins above 20%.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Small but high-margin and directly geared to compute density—an under-covered pure play on rack power growth.
insights.quote: thermal interface materials represent another attractive materials opportunity, with 2025 revenues of around $2 billion, a 10% CAGR to 2030, and greater than 20% EBITDA
insights.locator: Separately, thermal interface materials

insights.claim: Buying into resist sub-components—photoacid generators, stabilizers, specialty monomers, additives—gives diversified exposure across every major resist formulator instead of a bet on one finished product, with ultra-high purity sustaining the margins.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A picks-and-shovels-one-layer-deeper construct: own the input common to all competing resist platforms rather than picking the winning formulation.
insights.quote: Investing in this sub-sector would therefore provide diversified exposure to major resist formulators rather than reliance on the maker of a single finished product.
insights.locator: Sub-components of resists

insights.claim: Lithography clean and strip solutions have shorter qualification cycles and a more fragmented supplier landscape than leading resist products, making them the easier entry point for a new player despite tightening residue and defect-control requirements.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Counterintuitive entry map: the unglamorous cleans niche is more penetrable than resists—relevant to where new capital can actually win share.
insights.quote: qualification cycles are often shorter and the supplier landscape more fragmented, creating more entry opportunities for emerging players
insights.locator: Lithography clean and strip solutions

insights.claim: There is no universally best segment in electronic chemicals: attractiveness for M&A or organic expansion depends on the buyer's starting position, technical infrastructure, core capabilities, and customer and supplier access.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Cuts against the habit of chasing the fastest-growing niche; judge deal announcements by capability overlap, not by segment growth rate.
insights.quote: No single segment can be considered the best opportunity, as suitability for either M&A or organic expansion will depend on each chemical player’s starting position.
insights.locator: Mapping the Opportunity for Chemicals Companies

insights.claim: The barriers protecting electronic chemicals margins are high R&D, long qualification cycles, and deep tool-and-process integration between manufacturer and supplier, which together produce sticky relationships and co-development rather than price competition.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Explains margin durability: incumbency is defended by requalification cost, so revenue is far stickier than in commodity chemicals.
insights.quote: barriers to entry such as high R&D, long qualification cycles, and tool and process integration between manufacturers and suppliers that encourage “sticky” relationships and co-development
insights.locator: The electronic chemicals and materials segment is therefore emerging

insights.claim: In semiconductor materials, qualification attaches not just to a product formulation but to the manufacturing process and site, raw-material set, packaging and delivery system, analytical controls, and change-management regime—so aggressive post-merger integration can destroy the asset it just bought.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The core diligence risk in this M&A wave: synergy plans that consolidate sites or re-source raw materials can void customer qualifications and vaporize revenue.
insights.quote: qualification can be tied not only to the product formulation but also to the manufacturing process and site, raw-material set, packaging and delivery system, analytical controls, and change-management regime
insights.locator: Integrate into the target niche.

insights.claim: Acquirers in electronic chemicals should prioritize bolt-on deals that add already-qualified products, talent, or customer access inside one or two chosen niches, rather than broad entry across the space.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A discipline test for management teams: large diversifying deals here signal strategy drift, bolt-ons signal execution.
insights.locator: Acquire strategically.

insights.claim: Entegris has an enterprise value of around $20 billion—more than double its 2019 value—with EBITDA consistently exceeding 25%, after evolving from contamination control into a broad semiconductor materials and process-solutions platform.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The comp for what a successfully compounded electronic-materials platform is worth, and the margin bar peers must clear.
insights.locator: Entegris Demonstrates How Players Build and Scale

insights.claim: Entegris's three-step playbook was to establish a foothold in purity and contamination control to win fab access, expand into adjacencies sharing the same technology foundations and customers, then scale via acquisitions such as ATMI and CMC Materials while divesting to sharpen focus.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A replicable sequence for testing whether another chemicals company's semis strategy is credible: foothold, adjacency, then M&A scale plus pruning.
insights.locator: Its growth can be described as following a three-step playbook

themes.theme: Geopolitical fragility of the supply chain

insights.claim: Players in electronic chemicals should run scenario planning for tariffs, export controls, and localization requirements, treating geopolitical disruption as a base-case operating condition rather than a tail risk.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Policy shocks in semis inputs hit the materials layer too; scenario readiness and dual-qualified second sources are differentiators worth probing on earnings calls.
insights.locator: Fortify the position.

insights.claim: Because changing a manufacturing site can itself require customer approval or requalification, regionalizing production is not a quick fix for tariff or localization pressure and must be built into the qualification strategy in advance.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Second-order insight: onshoring announcements in electronic chemicals take years to convert into revenue—discount headline reshoring capex accordingly.
insights.quote: Because manufacturing-site changes can themselves require customer approval or requalification, regionalization should be incorporated deliberately into the qualification strategy.
insights.locator: Fortify the position.
